# awl

> A calm, beautiful, and fun writing environment for prose and light code. Native (Rust + wgpu + winit + glyphon) with a lighter browser build from one core. WYSIWYG Markdown, a playful caret, authored worlds, and no IDE machinery.

awl is for people who want to create Markdown files, especially people who enjoy writing and typing on keyboards. Native platform shortcuts receive first-class support; selectable keymaps and individual rebinding remain available. Desktop is primary, macOS is the design center, and offline single-player use is the permanent assumption.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Frank-P-Lu/awl-next/blob/main/README.md): what awl is, build & run, status, and font/license notes.
- [Philosophy](https://github.com/Frank-P-Lu/awl-next/blob/main/PHILOSOPHY.md): the identity, priorities, and product boundary — fun, beauty, calm; WYSIWYG plain text; offline single-player; no word-processor or IDE machinery.
- [Design](https://github.com/Frank-P-Lu/awl-next/blob/main/DESIGN.md): the visual and interaction contract — coherent worlds, typography, tactile performance, one-primary-task surfaces, and keyboard-native pointer support.
- [Themes](https://github.com/Frank-P-Lu/awl-next/blob/main/THEMES.md): the world contract — every measurable law a theme must satisfy, the ink-ladder / role-tint derivation, and the add-a-world process.
- [Worlds](https://github.com/Frank-P-Lu/awl-next/blob/main/WORLDS.md): the human reference for the fourteen theme worlds — each one's flavour, faces, and section-break ornament.

## Concepts

- [Earned expression](https://github.com/Frank-P-Lu/awl-next/blob/main/DESIGN.md): a world may be quiet, loud, colorful, or animated when its expression forms a coherent and beautiful environment for writing rather than novelty alone.
- [Syntax highlighting — Alabaster](https://github.com/Frank-P-Lu/awl-next/blob/main/docs/syntax.md): a code buffer keeps everything in the default ink and distinguishes only four quiet roles — comment, string, constant, and definition.
- [WYSIWYG markdown](https://github.com/Frank-P-Lu/awl-next/blob/main/PHILOSOPHY.md): reveal-on-cursor — if the caret is on that line, show the actual markdown; otherwise show the styled preview.

## Try it

- [Editor (web build)](/editor): the experimental `wasm32` / WebGPU browser build — renders, types, styles markdown live, switches themes, and survives a reload. A demo, not a shipped product.
